messages:
sam: Quick heads-up — in the last canary run I saw p99 jump when we increase microbatch size + use chunked token streaming with a 40ms flush. p95 stays fine but p99 tails spike ~3-4x. anyone else see this pattern?

tina: saw similar on my local repro yesterday. seems correlated with kernel selection flipping to the 'fallback' path for longer seqs. p99 spikes line up with a few requests hitting a different matmul kernel.

raj: did you capture profiler traces? kernel switch + KV cache misses would explain intermittent long tail. can you paste perf traces / timings?

sam: attaching condensed profiling snippet from the canary (trimmed):
```
# top stacks (aggregate)
matmul_generic_kernel 38%  (hot during p99)
attention_opt_kernel 22%
kv_cache_lookup 12%
sys_sched 6%
other 22%
```
p95 = 110ms, p99 = 420ms, throughput unchanged. microbatch_size=8, flush_interval_ms=40, seq_len_dist: 128/256/1024 mix.

mike: interesting — when microbatch increases we expect better throughput but tail can worsen if batching delays align badly with streaming flush boundaries. also kernel selector uses heuristics on seq_len distribution, so a rare long sequence can force a non-optimized kernel for a subset of requests.

infra-bot: perf-alert: canary-run/2026-02-26 detected p99 regression (+280ms) vs baseline. Link: https://perf.redwood/alerts/3321 :warning:

tina: one quick experiment — try lowering flush_interval to 10ms and keep microbatch=8 to see if streaming chunk latency reduces perceived tail. but that may hurt throughput.

sam: did that: flush=10ms -> p95 ~100ms, p99 ~210ms (much better) but overall token throughput down ~8%. so tradeoff confirmed.

raj: other idea: adaptive flush that clamps to observed queueing. e.g., if current in-flight microbatch < threshold, flush sooner; else wait to fill to microbatch. Also we should prefer fast kernel when sequence lengths in microbatch are homogeneous — might be worth grouping by seq_len bucket at admission.

mike: grouping by seq_len is neat but adds scheduling overhead and could fragment GPUs. maybe cheap hashing to put similar-length requests in same microbatch. also add a fast-path in kernel selector: if avg_seq_len in batch < 300 choose optimized kernel even if a single outlier exists, but guard with seq_pad_limit to avoid OOMs.

sam: noted. i also instrumented KV cache hit timing — on p99 traces the KV lookup sometimes stalls if concurrent eviction runs kick in. snippet: `kv_lookup_latency_ms = 0.6, but occasional stalls up to 120ms` — need metrics.

tina: can we move eviction to a low-priority thread or stagger it? or make eviction incremental so it doesn't hold locks long?

raj: yes, incremental GC for the cache. also add per-request KV lookup timeout so we don't stall model forward; treat missed KV as cold and continue generating (trade quality for latency).

sam: concrete proposal for next canary:
- experiment A: microbatch=8 + flush=10ms (baseline throughput impact)
- experiment B: microbatch=16 + adaptive_flush (flush sooner if batch incomplete for >15ms) + seq_len-bucket admission
- experiment C: microbatch=8 + evict-thread-priority-low + kv-lookup-timeout=50ms + prefer-optimized-kernel-heuristic
We'll run perf traces and compare p95/p99 + tokens/s and % of requests that hit fallback kernel.

mike: add a metric for "kernel_flip_rate" per-minute. Also capture per-chunk perceived latency (time from client-first-byte to first-token-flush). that maps to user-facing latency.

sam: agreed. also want to log when we pick generic kernel with `(reason=seq_outlier)` so we can tune the threshold.

infra-bot: scheduled: canary jobs for A/B/C start 2026-02-26T15:30Z. Results will be posted to #eng-runtime/perf after completion.

tina: one more tiny optimization: if a request is streaming and we've produced prefix tokens, flush smaller tail chunks (e.g., 8 tokens) immediately to keep perceived latency low while larger microbatch fills in background. reduces p99 for interactive flows.

sam: nice — call it "prefix-priority flush". let's add it to experiment C as opt-in.

raj: i'll draft the admission + kernel-heuristic change and a lightweight sim to predict p99 impact before canary.

mike: i'll wire the metrics + perf alert thresholds (we can auto-roll back if p99 regress >100ms over baseline).

sam: thanks team. will open PR with flags for A/B/C and attach the profiling traces. planning to land incremental GC + kv-timeout first then iterate. :thumbsup:
